title: Compatibility with finite reduction
statement: In the six-functor datum of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism, let $1\le m\le n$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_{E,n})$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. Write $K_m=K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ and $L_m=L\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ for their finite reductions. Then the square comparing $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ and $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ through the finite-reduction compatibilities of $Rf_!$, $-\otimes^L$ and $Lf^*$ commutes; hence $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ is.

proof.text: First check the coefficient domains, without invoking axioms (A3) or (A5) of the datum. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose bounded constructible étale representatives of $K,L$ and retain their comparison isomorphisms as étale-origin witnesses. By clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], the representatives have the same finite Tor amplitudes. The constructible variant of [lem-sf-flat-model] applies because $X,Y$ are finite type over a field, hence Noetherian: choose bounded flat constructible étale models $P,Q$. With $A=A_{E,n}$ and $B=A_{E,m}$, their termwise tensors with $B$ represent the derived reductions. Each term remains flat over $B$, since $(P^i\otimes_A B)\otimes_B N=P^i\otimes_A N$ for a $B$-module sheaf $N$ and restriction of scalars is exact; it remains constructible since on a common finite stratification its values are finite modules tensored with the finite ring $B$. Thus the reductions are bounded constructible and have finite Tor amplitude, with the same bounds. The same models show that $K\otimes_A^L Lf^*L$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude: inverse image is exact for constant coefficients, takes each flat locally constant term on a stratum to such a term on its inverse image, and the bounded total tensor model has amplitude bounded by the sums of the two intervals. Clause (i) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] returns these objects and their finite-Tor properties to the pro-étale site. All operations below are taken on these witnessed realizations.

Put $\rho_T=-\otimes_A^L B$ on each scheme $T$, and suppress the subscript when its scheme is determined. Let $c_f(M):\rho Rf_{!,A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}\rho M$ be [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], and let $s$ and $t$ denote the tensor and pullback comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Define $u$ by $\rho(Rf_{!,A}K\otimes_A^L L)\xrightarrow{s}\rho Rf_{!,A}K\otimes_B^L L_m\xrightarrow{c_f(K)\otimes1}Rf_{!,B}K_m\otimes_B^L L_m$. Define $v$ by $\rho Rf_{!,A}(K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L)\xrightarrow{c_f(K\otimes Lf_A^*L)}Rf_{!,B}\rho(K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L)\xrightarrow{Rf_{!,B}(s,t)}Rf_{!,B}(K_m\otimes_B^L Lf_B^*L_m)$. Both $u$ and $v$ are isomorphisms by the cited statements and the domains checked in step 1. The square to be proved is precisely
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
\rho(Rf_{!,A}K\otimes_A^L L)&\xrightarrow{\rho(\operatorname{PF}_{A})}&\rho Rf_{!,A}(K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L)\\
{\scriptstyle u}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle v}\\
Rf_{!,B}K_m\otimes_B^L L_m&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{B}}&Rf_{!,B}(K_m\otimes_B^L Lf_B^*L_m).
\end{array}
$$
In particular its upper arrow is the reduction of the level-$n$ map.

As before, $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [thm-nagata-compactification] gives $f=pj$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper. Put $M=j_!K$. Apply [lem-trf-open-ctf]: $M$ is bounded constructible with the same Tor bounds as $K$. Apply the same lemma to $K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L$, whose domain was checked in step 1. The open projection isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] identifies its extension by zero with $M\otimes_A^L Lp_A^*L$, using $Lj^*Lp^*=Lf^*$. This checks both proper-factor inputs. Their étale-origin witnesses are supplied by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin].

source.place: Opening comparison domains and the compactification used to construct PF

proof.text: By [def-exchange-projection] and [def-sf-pf], at either coefficient ring $R=A,B$ the specified map is $\operatorname{PF}_R=Rp_{*,R}(\gamma_R)\circ\pi_R$, with $\pi_R$ the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_R\otimes1)\circ\mu_R$. For proper $p$, the compactification $(\operatorname{id},p)$ identifies $Rp_!$ with $Rp_*$ by [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The canonical coefficient map $c_M:\rho Rp_{*,A}M\to Rp_{*,B}\rho M$ is the mate of $Lp_B^*\rho\cong\rho Lp_A^*$. More generally [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] pins the compact-support coefficient comparison for $f=pj$ to this proper mate followed by the canonical coefficient comparison for $j_!$. This is the same canonical tensor comparison $c_f$ used in step 2 [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. The domains checked in step 3 apply. Here $A,B$ are finite rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and $p,j,f$ are maps of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, as required.

source.place: Compactification factorization of PF and the coefficient comparison as a counit mate

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] with the four ringed topoi $(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. The vertical maps are $p_A,p_B$; the horizontal maps are the identity maps of the underlying topoi with structure-ring maps $A\to B$. Their derived pullbacks are $\rho_{\overline X},\rho_Y$. The square commutes as a square of ringed topoi, and its pullback comparison is exactly $t:Lp_B^*\rho_Y\cong\rho_{\overline X}Lp_A^*$. These are small sites in a common chosen universe. Its exchange map is the mate $c$ pinned in step 4, and its projection maps are precisely $\pi_A,\pi_B$, since all are defined using the same tensor comparison and counit. With inputs $E=M,Q=L$, its displayed equality therefore says
$$Rp_{*,B}(s,t)\circ c_{M\otimes Lp_A^*L}\circ\rho\pi_A
=\pi_B\circ(c_M\otimes1)\circ s.$$
The lemma requires no Cartesian hypothesis and no flatness of $B$ over $A$. This supplies the entire proper-factor mate calculation formerly inline.

source.place: Both transposes are the same counit-tensor composite: proper direct-image factor

proof.text:
For the open factor use [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] with $g=\operatorname{id}_{\overline X}$ and structure-ring map $A\to B$. Its $\beta$ is $d_H:\rho j_{!,A}H\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}\rho H$, and its $\gamma$ is the canonical open tensor identification at each level. Under these isomorphisms both the source and target of the desired identity are in the essential image of $j_{!,B}$. The lemma gives invertible open units and full faithfulness of extension by zero; hence restriction to the open is faithful between these objects. After restriction, its normalized $\beta$ and $\gamma$ become identities. The remaining tensor and pullback identifications are the canonical coherent ones of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], so both routes are the same tensor/pullback comparison, including $Lj^*Lp^*=Lf^*$. Faithfulness gives
$$d_{K\otimes Lf_A^*L}\circ\rho\gamma_A=\gamma_B\circ(d_K\otimes1)$$
with $s,t$ inserted on source and target. Thus the open compatibility follows from a cited normalization theorem, rather than an unproved assertion that its construction commutes with reduction.

source.place: The open-immersion tensor identification and coefficient reduction

proof.text: Compose the proper-factor identity of step 5 with the image by $Rp_{*,B}$ of the open-factor identity of step 6. Substitute $\operatorname{PF}_R=Rp_{*,R}(\gamma_R)\circ\pi_R$ and the proper-mate/open-comparison factorization of $c_f$ from step 4. Naturality of $c$ moves $\rho Rp_{*,A}(\gamma_A)$ past $c$; the two middle tensor/pullback identifications cancel. The resulting source composite is $\operatorname{PF}_B\circ u$, and the target composite is $v\circ\rho(\operatorname{PF}_A)$, using exactly the definitions of $u,v$ in step 2. Therefore the required square commutes. This is an equality of specified morphisms, established before any stalk or generating-class argument.

source.place: Compose the two compactification factors to obtain the specified reduction square

proof.text: The commutative square and the inverses of $u,v$ show that $\rho(\operatorname{PF}_A)$ is invertible if and only if $\operatorname{PF}_B$ is invertible. This cancellation concerns the reduced map. For the asserted equivalence with the original map, apply [thm-sf-pf-finite] at $A$ and $B$ to the étale representatives from step 1: both $\operatorname{PF}_A$ and $\operatorname{PF}_B$ are isomorphisms, so the claimed equivalence holds. For the pro-étale realizations use the witnessed-realization clause of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], which states precisely the same invertibility there. The representatives satisfy its bounded constructibility and finite-Tor hypotheses by step 1. This completes both the commutativity and the original-map invertibility assertion.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph: reduction square, mate comparison, and final invertibility sentence
